items.t: — LivePriceOfGold's Dubai board, timestamped 10 August at 10:07 UTC, reads AED 512.45 a gram for 24-carat gold and AED 470.43 for 22-carat. Goodreturns' Dubai page, dated the same day, reads AED 523.25 and AED 484.50, a gap of 2.11% and 2.99% respectively, both derived by this desk. The peg arithmetic on Kitco spot at $4,341.40 an ounce gives AED 512.59 a gram, which puts LivePriceOfGold on the raw-metal lane, AED 0.14 away, and Goodreturns AED 10.66 above it. Neither page is wrong; they publish different quantities under one label. Goodreturns' page stepped up AED 13.25 between 7 and 8 August against a metal move of AED 3.13 and has held flat for three days since

items.b: THE EDITOR'S READ IS THE MARK
items.t: — Under the one-price rule, the tape carries this desk's 5:57am New York reading of Kitco's live board on 10 August: gold $4,341.40, up $0.10 or 0.00% against Friday 7 August's close; silver $63.99, up 52.8 cents or 0.83%; platinum $1,737.00, down $6.00 or 0.34%; palladium $1,340.00, down $17.00 or 1.25%. The 4:58am tape had read $4,345.40, $64.06, $1,739.00 and $1,342.00; every previous close matches, so this is one open session moving between two reads and the fresher verified reading has been written back. Fine gold is $139.58 a gram and the gold-to-silver ratio narrows to 67.84 from 68.41

— India hallmarked 5.9 million silver articles in the 2025-26 financial year against 3.2 million the year before, an increase of about 84% derived by this desk, on Bureau of Indian Standards figures disclosed 9 August. About 230 recognised assaying and hallmarking centres handle silver testing; the recognised laboratory network has gone from 147 in 2014 to 440 and government-empanelled laboratories from 24 to 350, against ten standalone bureau laboratories and roughly 270,000 samples tested. Silver hallmarking has been voluntary since 2005 and no mandatory date has been set, though the unique identification number the regime would need was introduced for silver in September 2025. The bureau names the cause as consumers moving into silver because gold has become unaffordable

— Etsy is removing about 220 roles, roughly 12% of its marketplace workforce, mainly from product and engineering, at an estimated $35 million charge booked in the third quarter, leaving about 1,600 employees. The plan was disclosed 6 August alongside second-quarter revenue of $668.3 million, up 6.2% and ahead of a $646.1 million consensus, gross merchandise sales from continuing operations of $2.58 billion, Etsy-only GMS up 7.5%, a take rate of 25.9%, active sellers up 5.9% to 5.7 million and active buyers down 0.4% to 87.0 million. The company says the cut is neither a cost-reduction exercise nor related to artificial intelligence. Jewellery and personal accessories is one of the six largest categories by GMS in Etsy's own filings

— QVC Group formally exited Chapter 11 on 7 August, 113 days after filing on 16 April, a count derived by this desk from the two dates, having removed more than $5 billion of debt. It issued $1.2 billion of take-back notes due 2032 at a 10% coupon and secured a $600 million asset-based lending facility, with the equity approved for Nasdaq trading under QVCG. David Rawlinson, chief executive since 2021, stepped down; Mike George returns as interim chief executive and board chair alongside a new eight-member board. Fine and fashion jewellery has been among the top-selling categories on the platform

— Pandora named Paulo Garcia chief financial officer on 6 August. He joins 1 October and takes the role 1 December, succeeding Anders Boyer, who retires 30 November after more than fourteen years and stays until 31 March 2027 to hand over. Garcia arrives from the chief financial officer's seat at Walmart de Mexico y Centroamerica, a listed subsidiary with about $50 billion of revenue and 240,000 employees, and was previously chief financial officer for Europe and Indonesia at Ahold Delhaize and before that at Unilever. With Berta de Pablos-Barbier taking office as chief executive on 1 January and Andre Branch named North America president, three of the top seats at the largest jewellery company in the world by units turn over inside twelve months, and none of the three arrives from jewellery

— This paper printed three UAE retail gold readings for the 7 August session and declined to choose between them: Khaleej Times at AED 517.50 a gram, one bureau desk at AED 510.25 and another at AED 514.00. The peg arithmetic for that session gives AED 509.42, which places the 510.25 on the raw-metal lane and the 517.50 on the counter lane. The divergence this desk carried unresolved across three editions was a category error rather than a data error. The correction of understanding is recorded here rather than left in the archive; no published figure was wrong, and none has been altered

items.b: DIAMONDS DARK ON VERIFICATION, NOT ON ABSENCE
items.t: — The rough desk filed seven items and none survived the archive check: De Beers' 88% second-quarter production rise ran here 24 July, Gem Diamonds' Letšeng half-year ran 29 July, the RapNet index rebound ran 4 August, Antwerp's half-year ran 8 August, the Belgium-India tariff gap has run five times since 8 July, and a lab-grown stabilisation figure was recycled from sourcing this paper already rejected on 31 July. A seventh, an Alrosa price signal, traces to an article dated 26 March 2026 and filed as August news. The Editor's own diamonds sweep returned only stale or already-published material. Third consecutive dark diamonds edition

items.b: WHAT ELSE DID NOT PRINT TODAY
items.t: — Three more slate items were killed on date. Brilliant Earth's second quarter, ranked the day's strongest item, published here on 7 August as twenty-two-thirty-eight-an-order with the identical $115.1 million, 5.7% rise, $2,238 average order value, 57.9% gross margin and $459-462 million guidance; killed as a repeat. Pandora's lab-grown expansion to Spain and Italy carries a release date of 25 June with the Barcelona and Milan flagships opened 12 and 26 June, and the Pandora Wonders platform with Harry Lambert launched 8-9 July at Paris Couture Week; the company's newsroom index lists both under today's date, which is a page artefact rather than a publication date. Van Cleef & Arpels' first Madrid boutique opened 11 April, four months before the 7 August press release that surfaced it. The Chinese brand-counter spread was pulled: the aggregators returned stale or empty cells again and this desk will not print a counter price it cannot verify. Gemstones is dark for a sixth consecutive edition, watches and auctions for the first. Sotheby's Arcade Hong Kong closed 6 August and has published no result for a fifth day. RAPI returned 403 for a sixth day and the Zimnisky rough index remains unreadable; NAT1 and LGD1 both carry unchanged
